title: The supported pairing recipe
statement:
Fix the coefficient conventions of
[def-trf-coefficient-conventions], $A=A_{E,n}$, $s=\Spec k$. Let
$X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes whose structure morphisms
$a_X,a_Y$ are exceptionally admissible
([def-trf-admissibility]), with the dualizing data
$\omega_X,\omega_Y$, $D_X,D_Y$ and evaluations of
[def-trf-dualizing-complex], and let
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$. Put

$$
Z:=Y\times_sX,\qquad p_1:Z\to Y,\quad p_2:Z\to X,
$$

and let $\tau:X\times_sY\xrightarrow{\sim}Y\times_sX$ exchange the
factors. External products are
$M\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}N:=Lp_1^*M\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}Lp_2^*N$
([def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]).

*Opposite pairs.* Let $(C,c,u)$ be a correspondence from $(X,K)$ to
$(Y,L)$ and $(D,d,v)$ an opposite correspondence, in the sense of
[def-trf-correspondence-between-pairs] (which generalizes
[def-trf-correspondence], the case $(Y,L)=(X,K)$); such a pair is an
*opposite pair*. With $\bar d=\tau d:D\to Z$ and
$E=E(C,D)=C\times_{c,Z,\bar d}D$ as there, write $e_C:E\to C$,
$e_D:E\to D$ for the projections and
$e:=c\,e_C=\bar d\,e_D:E\to Z$ (all maps separated of finite type, and
exceptionally admissible where an exceptional functor is applied; in
particular $c$, $\bar d$, $e$, both product projections, and the
structure morphisms $a_Z=a_Yp_1$ and $a_E=a_Ze$ are exceptionally
admissible, as provided by [def-trf-admissibility]).

*Step 1: the supported classes.* Let
$[u]\in H^0_C\bigl(Z,\RHom_A(Lp_2^*K,Rp_1^!L)\bigr)$ be the class of
$u$ given by [lem-trf-correspondence-class], a class supported on $c$
in the sense of [def-trf-supported-class].
The Künneth–Verdier
isomorphism of [thm-trf-kunneth-verdier] for the product $Y\times_sX$,
with $M=L$ and $N=K$,
$\kappa_{L,K}:L\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}D_XK\xrightarrow{\sim}
\RHom_A(Lp_2^*K,Rp_1^!L)$, gives the class supported on $c$

$$
\widetilde u:=\kappa_{L,K}^{-1}\circ[u]:
Rc_!A_C\longrightarrow P:=L\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}D_XK .
$$

For the opposite correspondence, put $W=X\times_sY$ and let
$q_1:W\to X$, $q_2:W\to Y$ be its projections.
Apply [lem-trf-correspondence-class] with $(X,K)$ and $(Y,L)$
interchanged to obtain
$[v]:Rd_!A_D\to\RHom_A(Lq_2^*L,Rq_1^!K)$.
Then [thm-trf-kunneth-verdier] with $M=K$, $N=L$ gives
$\kappa_{K,L}^{-1}\circ[v]:Rd_!A_D\to K\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}D_YL$.
Apply $R\tau_!$ to this morphism. Since $\tau$ is an isomorphism,
$R\tau_!=R\tau_*$ and $R\tau_*\simeq L(\tau^{-1})^*$;
composition in [prop-functor-package], item (3), identifies its
source with $R\bar d_!A_D$. The identities
$q_1\tau^{-1}=p_2$ and $q_2\tau^{-1}=p_1$, together with
[lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso], identify its target with
$Lp_2^*K\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}Lp_1^*D_YL$.
Compose with the signed tensor symmetry to obtain

$$
\widetilde v:R\bar d_!A_D\longrightarrow Q:=D_YL\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}K .
$$

*Step 2: the support of the product.* The projection formula
([prop-functor-package], item (5)), the base change
$Lc^*R\bar d_!\simeq Re_{C!}Le_D^*$ in the Cartesian square defining
$E$ ([prop-functor-package], item (4)), and the composition
$Rc_!Re_{C!}\simeq Re_!$ ([prop-functor-package], item (3)) give the
canonical isomorphism below. Here $Le_D^*A_D\simeq A_E$
by constant-coefficient pullback, and the projection formula is used
for $f=c$, with its two inputs $A_C$ and $R\bar d_!A_D$. The
latter belongs to $D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$ by [def-trf-admissibility],
since $A_D$ is the finite free rank-one coefficient object. Insert
the tensor unit $A_C$ in $Rc_!(Lc^*R\bar d_!A_D)$ and apply the
inverse of item (5) to get the last arrow:

$$
\mu:Re_!A_E\simeq Rc_!Re_{C!}Le_D^*A_D
\simeq Rc_!\bigl(Lc^*R\bar d_!A_D\bigr)
\simeq Rc_!A_C\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}R\bar d_!A_D .
$$

*Step 3: the pairing.* Write $T_1=Lp_1^*L$,
$T_2=Lp_2^*D_XK$, $T_3=Lp_1^*D_YL$ and
$T_4=Lp_2^*K$. Reassociate the four factors of
$P\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}Q$ in the order
$(T_1,T_2,T_3,T_4)$. Move $T_3$ past
$T_2$ and then past $T_1$, using the signed tensor symmetries,
to obtain $(T_3,T_1,T_2,T_4)$.
On homogeneous factors of degrees $(a,b,c,d)$ this permutation has
sign $(-1)^{c(a+b)}$. Apply the inverses of the pullback/tensor
comparisons of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] separately
for $p_1$ and $p_2$. Thus
$P\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}Q\simeq
Lp_1^*(D_YL\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}L)\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}
Lp_2^*(D_XK\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}K)$; the two Verdier evaluations
$\operatorname{ev}_L$, $\operatorname{ev}_K$ of
[def-trf-dualizing-complex] map this to
$\omega_Y\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}\omega_X$, and the exceptional
Künneth isomorphism $\alpha$ of [prop-trf-exceptional-kunneth] for
$f_1=a_Y$, $f_2=a_X$, $L_1=L_2=A_s$ (note $a_Y\times a_X=a_Z$ and
$A_s\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}A_s=A_s$ on $s\times_ss=s$) is the product
comparison $\omega_Y\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}\omega_X\simeq\omega_Z$.
Here $\alpha$ is the specified map of [def-sf-kv-maps] (ii): the
exceptional adjoint of $\mathrm{Ku}_!$ followed by the two counits
$Ra_{Y!}\omega_Y\to A_s$ and $Ra_{X!}\omega_X\to A_s$; thus the
product comparison is a specified morphism, not a choice of an
isomorphism between its source and target.
Composing,

$$
\sigma_{u,v}:
Re_!A_E\xrightarrow{\ \mu\ }
Rc_!A_C\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}R\bar d_!A_D
\xrightarrow{\widetilde u\otimes\widetilde v}
P\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}Q
\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_L\boxtimes\operatorname{ev}_K}
\omega_Y\boxtimes_A^{\mathrm L}\omega_X
\xrightarrow{\ \alpha\ }\omega_Z .
$$

The *Borel–Moore section*

$$
\langle u,v\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}:A_E\longrightarrow\omega_E
$$

is the exceptional adjoint of $\sigma_{u,v}$, using the adjunction
of [def-trf-admissibility]: its image under
$\Hom_Z(Re_!A_E,\omega_Z)\cong\Hom_E(A_E,Re^!\omega_Z)$, followed by
the identification $Re^!\omega_Z\simeq\omega_E$ of
[thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition].

*The diagonal case.* For $(Y,L)=(X,K)$ take the opposite
correspondence $D=X$, $d=\Delta_X$, $v=1_K$ (both legs are
$\operatorname{id}_X$); then $\bar d=\Delta_X$ and
$E=C\times_{X\times_sX,c,\Delta_X}X=\Fix(c)$ is the fixed scheme of
[def-trf-fixed-scheme]. Abbreviate
$\LT_B(u,v)=\LT_B(\langle u,v\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}})$, the local term of
[def-trf-local-term] (for $B$ a proper open-and-closed component),
namely $\int_B j_B^*\langle u,v\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}$ using the
integration of [def-trf-integration].

split_report.summary: Audited the definition against the current main-20261015 blueprint, all fifteen original dependency statements, and the existing Lean pairing construction. Adopted blueprint_update.statement, removing its obsolete forward trace-class assertion. Named the existing pro-etale pullback/tensor comparison and the canonical exceptional Kunneth map definition, and made the already automatic admissibility of the product and intersection structure maps explicit. All ingredients already exist: no new nodes or Mathlib leaves. This is a definition, so proof and proof_deps remain empty; its construction is in the statement and all its ingredients are statement dependencies. Second reading expanded the opposite-class construction, the exact projection-formula inputs and their finite-Tor justification, and the signed tensor permutation. It also named the final adjunction and confined the integration citation to the proper component. Repair: rebased against the landed split of def-trf-local-term and re-read its unchanged statement, confirming the proper-B local-term use and no properness requirement on E. Fresh second reading independently revalidated all seventeen current dependency statements, particularly the landed local-term definition named in the return, and retained the construction unchanged; added independent Mathlib search records and the current second-reading report.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the entire current def-trf-supported-pairing construction: opposite pair, Step 1 supported classes via inverse Kunneth–Verdier, Step 2 the intersection-support isomorphism, Step 3 evaluation and the canonical product dualizing map, exceptional adjunction and the diagonal specialization. sk-d-pairing states the same recipe in shorthand; its display Q=K boxtimes D_Y L on Y times X has factors in the wrong order, whereas this node uses the correctly typed Q=D_Y L boxtimes K. The separate sk-d-pairing key node owns the unit-realization fields.
